scenarios.title: {Pf} Doesn't Want to Be Seen
text: {Pf} has asked {J}, again, not to post photos of her. A fan account found her old profile anyway and has been reposting her holiday pictures.
Fans keep asking who {J}'s mystery girlfriend is. {Pf} wants to keep it that way. {J}'s agent says 'a couple photo would be great for engagement'.

choices.label: Protect her privacy completely
choices.text: He asks fan accounts to respect her privacy. Most do. {Pf} reads his post three times and hugs him at the door that night.

choices.label: One tasteful photo, her back to the camera
choices.text: She agrees, reluctantly. The photo is lovely. The comments find her anyway. She goes quiet for a day.

choices.label: Ask the fan accounts to stop
choices.text: Most delete the photos. One doesn't, and gets 10,000 new followers for being 'brave'. The internet is strange.

scenarios.title: {Pf} the Influencer
text: {Pf}'s own following has exploded since they got together. Brands want her. She wants {J} in her videos. Lots of them.
{Pf} has been offered her own TV show about 'life as a footballer's partner'. She's thrilled. She wants him to appear in the first episode.

choices.label: Be her co-star
choices.text: The videos are funny and genuine. Her career takes off. His teammates send him the clips with crying-laughing emojis.

choices.label: Support her, stay off camera
choices.text: He's her biggest fan from behind the camera. She appreciates it. She'd love more.

choices.label: Ask her to slow down
choices.text: 'Can we be a bit less public?' Her face closes. 'You're public every weekend in front of thousands of people.'

scenarios.title: Long Distance
text: Time zones are winning. {J}'s evenings are {Pf}'s early mornings. Their calls get shorter. Tonight, she fell asleep mid-sentence.
{Pf} sends a voice note: 'I miss you in a way that's starting to feel permanent.' He listens to it on the team bus four times.

out.text: She says yes, after a week of thinking. She quits her job. The first month in a new country is hard for her, and good for them.
She says no. Her career, her family, her life. 'Why is it always me who has to move?'

choices.label: Fly her out every month
choices.text: {cost} a month in flights. Every visit is a holiday. Every goodbye is an airport.

choices.label: Schedule calls properly
choices.text: Nine o'clock every night, his time. Her morning coffee, his bedtime tea. It becomes a ritual.

scenarios.title: The Ring
text: {J} has been carrying a ring in his kitbag for three weeks. He keeps planning the perfect moment and chickening out.
{MUM} has asked, again, when he's going to 'make it official' with {Pf}. {J} has already bought the ring. Nobody knows.

choices.label: On the pitch, after a match

out.text: The stadium screen shows it live. She says yes. Thirty thousand people cheer. It's the most romantic thing the club has ever filmed.
She says yes — and then, in the car, says she wishes it had been just them. Whether she'll forgive the crowd depends on her.

choices.label: Somewhere private and meaningful
choices.text: At {PLACE}, where they first met, with nobody watching. She cries. He cries. A waiter cries. It's perfect.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: The ring goes back in the bag. {Pf} doesn't know it exists. She does wonder, sometimes, where this is going.

scenarios.title: The Wedding
text: The wedding is set for the off-season. The guest list is a war: {MUM} wants four hundred people, {Pf} wants sixty, the club wants a magazine deal.
Wedding planning. {Pf}'s family, {J}'s family, two cultures, one day. The seating chart has caused three arguments and one tear.

choices.label: Huge, traditional, everyone invited
choices.text: Four hundred guests, three days of celebration, {DAD} dancing for the first time in twenty years. It costs {cost}. Nobody remembers the cost.

choices.label: Small and private
choices.text: Sixty people in a garden. No cameras. An aunt who wasn't invited calls it 'a scandal'. {Pf} calls it perfect.

choices.label: Sell the photos to a magazine
choices.text: The magazine pays more than the wedding cost. The photos are beautiful. Some guests feel like extras in an advert.

scenarios.title: Big News
text: {Pf} is waiting at the door when he gets home from training. She's holding something behind her back. She's been crying, the good kind.
The test is positive. {Pf} shows him the little plastic stick and they both stare at it like it might change its mind.
scenarios.prompt: You're going to be a father.

choices.label: Tell the world
choices.text: Next goal, he puts the ball up his shirt and sucks his thumb. The stadium works it out in about two seconds.

choices.label: Keep it private for now
choices.text: They tell their parents on a video call. {MUM} screams so loudly the call disconnects.

scenarios.title: The Baby Arrives
text: The call comes at 4am the night before an away match: it's time. The hospital is three hours away. The team bus leaves at nine.
{Pf} goes into labour on a Thursday. The match is on Saturday. {Mf} has already said 'go'.

choices.label: Be there, miss the match
choices.hint: Some things are bigger than football.
choices.text: He holds his child for the first time at 7:12am. He doesn't see the match. He doesn't care. {Mf} sends a photo of the whole squad holding up a sign: 'WELCOME LITTLE ONE'.

choices.label: Play, then rush to the hospital

out.text: He plays, scores, and makes it to the hospital in time — just. He'll tell this story forever.
He misses it by forty minutes. {Pf} forgives him. She also mentions it at every family gathering for the rest of their lives.

scenarios.title: Fatherhood
text: The baby hasn't slept more than two hours in a row for a week. Neither has {J}. In training, he falls asleep on the physio's table.
His child grabbed his finger and smiled at him today. He played the best game of his month that weekend and doesn't think it's a coincidence.

choices.label: Take the night shifts
choices.text: He does every other night. {Pf} gets to sleep. He trains on fumes and is happier than he's ever been.

choices.label: Hire a night nurse
choices.text: A night nurse costs {cost} a month and gives them back their sleep. {Pf} cries with relief.

choices.label: Ask the grandparents to come
choices.text: {MUM} arrives with two suitcases and takes over completely. The baby sleeps. Everyone else argues about how to fold tiny socks.

scenarios.title: A First Date, Watched
text: {J} has a first date with {F}. Within ten minutes, three tables are filming them. By dessert, a gossip account has posted a blurry photo.
Coffee with {F}, someone {J} met through {BFf}. The barista recognises him, and so does everyone in the queue.
scenarios.prompt: The world is watching your date.

choices.label: Laugh about it with her
choices.desc: Make it part of the date.
choices.hint: If she can handle this, she can handle anything.

out.text: She finds it hilarious and waves at the cameras. They leave through the kitchen, giggling. A second date is arranged before the first one ends.
She's polite, but clearly uncomfortable. 'Is it always like this?' He has to say yes. There's no second date.

choices.label: Leave and go somewhere private
choices.text: They cook pasta badly at his apartment and talk until 2am. It's the best night he's had in ages. Her name is {F}.

choices.label: Call it off
choices.text: He apologises and ends it early. Being famous is lonely in ways he didn't expect.

scenarios.title: An Ex Reappears
text: {F}, an ex from before he was famous, messages: she's in town, she'd love to catch up. Just coffee. Her timing is suspicious, her message very warm.
At a friend's party, {J} runs into {F}, the girl he dated at seventeen. She's even more charming than he remembers.

out.text: Two hours of nostalgia. It's nice. That's all it is. But a fan photographs them laughing.
Coffee is just coffee. Nobody sees. Good to close that chapter properly.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: 'Good to hear from you, take care.' He means it. He doesn't reply again.

choices.label: Tell your partner about it first
choices.text: He tells {Pf} before deciding. Whatever she says, she remembers that he told her.

scenarios.title: {Pf} and {MUM}
text: {Pf} and {MUM} don't get along. {MUM} criticises the cooking. {Pf} criticises {MUM}'s criticism. {J} is in the middle, as always.
{MUM} has made a comment about {Pf}'s family at dinner. {Pf} is very, very quiet in the car home.

choices.label: Back {Pf}
choices.text: He tells {MUM}, kindly but firmly, that it's not okay. {MUM} sulks for a week. {Pf} kisses him on the forehead.

choices.label: Back {MUM}
choices.text: 'She didn't mean it like that.' {Pf} looks at him like she's seeing someone new.

choices.label: Get them in a room together

ok.text: Three hours, two pots of tea, one cooking lesson. They end up laughing at him. Allies, against him. Perfect.

bad.text: It's a disaster. Everyone leaves angry, including him.

scenarios.title: Did You Forget?
text: {Pf} is dressed up when he gets home. Candles on the table. He has no idea why. Then he remembers: their anniversary.
A message from {Pf}: 'Happy anniversary ❤️'. He has no gift, no plan, and a team meeting in twenty minutes.

choices.label: Confess and make it up big
choices.text: 'I forgot. I'm an idiot.' She laughs, a bit. The weekend trip he books for {cost} helps a lot.

ok.text: He improvises a picnic on the empty training pitch at sunset, thanks to a groundsman who owes him. She never finds out it was improvised.

bad.text: The 'surprise' is a takeaway from a petrol station. She knows. He knows she knows.

scenarios.title: Too Friendly
text: At a team event, {T} spends a lot of time talking to {Pf}. A lot. Laughing. She seems to enjoy it. {J} has noticed. So has half the squad.
{T} has started following {Pf} on social media and liking her old photos. It's probably nothing. It's probably not nothing.

choices.label: Talk to {Pf}
choices.hint: Depends on how you say it.

out.text: She laughs. '{T}? He was telling me about his dog for an hour.' Relief.
She's offended he even asked. 'Do you not trust me?' A long night.

choices.label: Confront {T}
choices.text: The confrontation is short and loud. {T} says he was just being friendly. Maybe he was. The squad takes sides.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: He lets it go. It was nothing. Trust, it turns out, feels better than suspicion.

scenarios.title: {Pf} Has Had Enough
text: {Pf} is sitting on the sofa with her coat still on when he gets home. 'We need to talk.' Four words that fill the room.
{Pf}'s bag is packed and waiting by the door. She hasn't left. Yet. 'Tell me why I should stay.'
scenarios.prompt: Your relationship is at breaking point.

choices.label: Promise real change
choices.text: He talks for two hours about what he's been doing wrong. She listens. She stays. For now, it's enough. It has to be more than words now.

choices.label: Suggest couples counselling
choices.text: She's surprised. Then relieved. The sessions are hard and honest. They help.

choices.label: Let her go
choices.text: He doesn't fight. She leaves. The apartment is very quiet. He sits in it for a long time.

scenarios.title: This Is It
text: Lying on the sofa, {Pf}'s head on his shoulder, a terrible film on TV, {J} realises he's completely, uncomplicatedly happy.
{Pf} knows him better than anyone ever has. She knows when to talk and when to just pass him the ice pack. It scares him a little, in the best way.

choices.label: Tell her exactly that
choices.text: He says it. She smiles without opening her eyes. 'I know.' Then: 'Me too.'

choices.label: Write it down
choices.text: He writes it on paper, badly, crossing out words. She keeps the letter in her jewellery box for the rest of her life.

scenarios.title: After the Breakup
text: The apartment still smells like her. Her toothbrush is in the bathroom. He hasn't moved it. He's not ready to move it.
Everybody has advice. {BFf} says 'get back out there'. {MUM} says 'eat something'. The squad says nothing, which is kindest.

choices.label: Lean on your friends
choices.text: {BFf} flies in. They watch bad films and eat {FOOD} and don't talk about her. Then they do. It helps.

choices.label: Throw yourself into football
choices.desc: Work it out on the pitch.
choices.text: Extra sessions every day. He's never been fitter. He's never been sadder. Both things are true.

choices.label: Go out every night
choices.text: Nightclubs, new faces, the gossip pages. None of it helps. All of it costs.

scenarios.title: Married Life
text: Married life is less romantic and more logistics: who's picking up what, whose parents are visiting, why there are seventeen pairs of football boots in the hallway.
{Pf} has made a shared calendar. It has colour codes. Football is red. Everything else is a slightly accusing shade of grey.

choices.label: Weekly date night, no exceptions
choices.text: Every Tuesday, no phones, no football. It's sometimes a picnic on the living-room floor. It's always theirs.

choices.label: Surprise trip in the next break
choices.text: Three days away, somewhere neither of them has been. They feel like they did at the start.

choices.label: It's fine as it is
choices.text: Comfortable. Familiar. Slightly too quiet some evenings.

scenarios.title: {Pf} During the Injury
text: {J} is grumpy, bored and on crutches. {Pf} has been carrying everything for weeks: shopping, driving, his bad moods.
The injury has made {J} unbearable. {Pf} has started taking long walks 'for some air'.

choices.label: Thank her properly
choices.text: He hobbles to the kitchen and makes her breakfast, badly, on one leg. She laughs so hard she has to sit down.

choices.label: Tell her to take a break
choices.text: He books her a weekend with her friends. She hesitates, then goes. She comes back lighter, and kinder to him.

choices.label: Keep sulking
choices.text: He sulks. She notices. The silence in the apartment gets heavier.

scenarios.title: Where Would We Live?
text: {J} might be sold. {Pf} has just started a job she loves. She asks the question he's been avoiding: 'If you go, do I have to go too?'
Transfer rumours, and {Pf} is googling cities. She's found the cost of rent in three of them and is very quiet.

choices.label: 'We decide together.'
choices.text: They make a list together: where she could work, where they'd both be happy. It doesn't solve anything. It changes everything.

choices.label: 'Football comes first. It always has.'
choices.hint: True, maybe. She won't forget it.
choices.text: She nods slowly. 'Okay. Then I need to think about what comes first for me.'

scenarios.title: Meeting the Parents
text: It's time for {Pf} to meet {MUM} and {DAD}. {MUM} has cooked for three days. {DAD} has ironed a shirt. {SIB} has prepared embarrassing stories.
{J} is meeting {Pf}'s parents. Her father is a quiet man who doesn't like football. He has a firm handshake and a long stare.

choices.label: Prepare like a cup final
choices.text: He brings the perfect gift, eats three helpings and asks good questions. Even the quiet father laughs once. {Pf} squeezes his hand under the table.

out.text: Relaxed and funny. Everyone gets on. {SIB} tells the story about him crying at a cartoon. He survives.
Too relaxed. A joke lands badly. The quiet father stares. The drive home is long.

scenarios.title: Power Couple
text: Magazines are calling {J} and {Pf} 'the power couple of the season'. Brands want them together. Paparazzi want them always.
{Pf} and {J} are on the cover of a lifestyle magazine. His teammates have stuck it all over the dressing room.

choices.label: Lean into it
choices.text: Red carpets, campaigns, a joint deal. Their bank account grows. So does the number of nights out before matches.

choices.label: Keep it to a minimum
choices.text: They say yes to one campaign and no to the rest. {Pf} is a little disappointed. {Mf} is relieved.
